title: Equator Finder: Where the Line Runs
description: Use the Equator Finder to see where 0° latitude crosses land, which countries it touches and how far your place sits from it. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the equator crosses Ecuador, Brazil, Indonesia, Uganda and Kenya — and passes just 20 km south of Quito, the capital named after the line itself.
quick_answer: The Equator Finder highlights Earth's 0-degree latitude line on the map and shows how far any place sits from it. Search or click to compare your location with the midline that divides the northern and southern hemispheres and anchors every latitude on the planet.

faq: Which countries does the equator pass through?

Thirteen by the usual count: Ecuador, Colombia and Brazil in South America; Gabon, the Republic of Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Somalia in Africa; and Indonesia and Kiribati among the island nations, plus São Tomé and Príncipe's islet of Rolas.
Is the equator a real line on the ground?
No paint, no fence — it is a coordinate, the great circle everywhere 0° latitude. Monuments mark it, and a few are a few hundred metres off because older surveys were less precise than GPS.
About 40,075 km (24,901 miles) — Earth's equatorial circumference on WGS84, slightly longer than the polar circumference of about 40,008 km because the planet bulges at the middle.
Why is it hot near the equator?
Sunlight arrives nearly vertically there year-round, concentrating energy per square metre. Distance from the line — not the line itself — is what drives the climate gradient.
Do days last 12 hours on the equator?
Nearly: daylight stays within a few minutes of 12 hours all year at 0°, because the Sun's path is almost perpendicular to the horizon in every season.
Can the Sun be directly overhead?
Yes, twice a year at the equinoxes (around March 20 and September 22–23), when the Sun's declination is 0°. Between the tropics it happens on other dates too.
Does water drain differently on each side?
No — that is a fairground myth. The Coriolis effect is real but far too weak at sink scale; demonstrations near equator monuments are showmanship, not physics.
What is the bulge at the equator about?
Rotation flings mass outward: the equatorial radius is about 6,378 km versus 6,357 km at the poles. That 21 km difference is why the equator is the longest latitude line.
